name: On the Self-Verification Limitations of Large Language Models on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
authors: Kaya Stechly, Karthik Valmeekam, Subbarao Kambhampati (Arizona State University)
venue: ICLR 2025 (Poster); arXiv preprint 2402.08115 first submitted Feb 2024
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (LLM critiques/backprompts its own answers) contrasted against tool-verified external sound verification; the paper is a critique/analysis of self-critique rather than a new method
feedback_source: Two regimes compared: (1) self-generated critique (LLM-as-verifier, the 'LLM+LLM' setup) and (2) external sound verifiers/ground-truth-oracle: VAL for STRIPS planning, SymPy symbolic checker for Game of 24, and a constraint/edge checker for graph coloring
iteration_structure: iterative-refine via repeated backprompting: a proposed answer is verified, and if rejected the critique is appended and the model re-queried, looping up to a stopping condition (e.g. 15 rounds); also compares against single-pass sampling (k=15, k=25)
reflection_object: output content / final answer (the proposed solution: a Game-of-24 arithmetic expression, a graph coloring assignment, or a STRIPS plan). The system reflects on and re-generates the candidate solution given a verdict/critique; it does not modify weights, prompts, skills, or reasoning-chain structure
requires_training: none (inference-time iterative prompting of a frozen GPT-4; no weight updates)
reward_or_critic_model: Contrasts self-as-judge (LLM critiquing itself, which collapses performance) against verifiable reward / sound external verifiers (SymPy, VAL, constraint checker) that provide guaranteed-correct verdicts and yield gains
distillation_target: none (no reusable artifact is distilled; this is an analysis of in-context iterative prompting with no memory or skill persistence)
emergent_vs_engineered: Studies prompt/scaffold-engineered reflection (Reflexion/Self-Refine/Tree-of-Thoughts-style iterative self-critique on GPT-4). It is not about RL-emergent reflection; it argues such engineered self-critique does not work without sound external verification
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad — the backprompt loop accumulates the history of failed attempts and critiques within a single task episode's context window; no long-term or cross-task memory
memory_persistence: within-episode (the failed-attempt history and critiques persist only across iterations of the same problem instance; nothing carries across tasks)
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only — each round appends the latest critique/failed attempt to the prompt; the authors note prompts grow additively with iteration (whereas sampling's token cost is quadratically lower)
error_localization_granularity: response-level / holistic outcome-level — the verifier renders a verdict on the whole proposed solution; critique variants range from binary feedback (B.F., just 'wrong') to first-error feedback (F.E.F., e.g. first wrong edge/action) to all-error feedback (A.E.F., every wrong edge/action), but the unit corrected is the full candidate answer
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task — iterative refinement within a single problem instance (Self-Refine/Reflexion-within-task style); no transfer of experience across tasks
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision — a complete candidate is generated, then verified and (if rejected) re-generated; no mid-trajectory in-flight correction. With self-critique this revision degrades performance; with a sound verifier it recovers/improves
task_domains: QA/reasoning, constraint-satisfaction, and planning/decision-making: arithmetic puzzle (Game of 24), graph coloring (NP-complete CSP), and STRIPS classical planning (Blocksworld and obfuscated Mystery Blocksworld)
benchmarks: Game of 24, Graph Coloring (custom generated instances), and STRIPS planning via Blocksworld and Mystery Blocksworld (PlanBench-style); sound verifiers: SymPy (Game of 24), constraint checker (Graph Coloring), VAL (planning)
headline_result: GPT-4 self-critique (LLM+LLM) causes performance collapse vs single-pass standard prompting: Game of 24 5% -> 3%, Graph Coloring 16% -> 2%, Mystery Blocksworld 4% -> 0% (Blocksworld modestly rose 40% -> 55%). Replacing the LLM verifier with a SOUND external verifier yields large gains: Game of 24 to 36-38%, Graph Coloring to 34-38%, Blocksworld to 60-87%, Mystery Blocksworld to ~6-10%. Critique content barely matters: binary/first-error/all-error feedback give similar results, and pure sampling+sound verifier (no critique) matches or beats it (e.g. Blocksworld k=25 sampling 72%)
baselines: Standard prompting single-pass (S.P.), self-consistency over 15 samples (S.C.), and plain sampling (k=15, k=25) re-checked by a sound verifier; the full LLM-self-critique pipeline (LLM+LLM with B.F./F.E.F./A.E.F. critique variants); also compared to Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT) cost/accuracy on Game of 24
gains_vs_baseline: Self-critique is net-negative vs S.P. in 3 of 4 domains (Game of 24 -2pp, Graph Coloring -14pp, Mystery Blocksworld -4pp). Sound external verifier is net-positive: Game of 24 +31 to +33pp (5%->36-38%), Graph Coloring +18 to +22pp (16%->34-38%), Blocksworld +20 to +47pp (40%->60-87%). Sampling+sound-verifier without any critique attains comparable gains, and self-consistency gives essentially no improvement over S.P.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time API-call multiplier with no training cost. Iterative backprompting prompts grow additively with iteration count; sampling-based prompts are quadratically cheaper. CoT verification raises Game-of-24 verifier accuracy 87%->99% but at ~17x output-token increase (more than doubling verification cost) and still leaves a 6pp gap to a sound verifier. ToT averages $0.74/problem (~150 CoT prompts); 150 direct queries + sound verifier reach 70% vs ToT's reported 74%
known_limitations: Self-critique fails because the LLM verifier has a high false-negative rate (rejecting valid solutions) and hallucinated critiques (non-existent edges in graph coloring, hallucinated precondition satisfaction in planning, incorrect rejections in Game of 24). Gains require a SOUND external verifier; results are GPT-4-specific on three formal/well-specified domains, so generalization to open-ended tasks and to reasoning models is not established. The content of critiques does not drive improvement
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier (sound, guaranteed-correct: SymPy, VAL, constraint checker) is required for gains; intrinsic self-verification is shown to be insufficient/harmful. THE discriminating finding: self-correction works only when verification comes from a sound external source, not from the LLM itself
self_correction_efficacy: net-negative for intrinsic self-critique (correction degrades performance in 3 of 4 domains and as backprompts increase quality consistently drops); net-positive only when paired with a sound external verifier. Effectively requires-oracle/sound-verifier; without label/verifier soundness it does not improve
calibration_effect: degrades — the verifier LLM is miscalibrated, with significant false-negative rates (e.g. Graph Coloring FNR 95.8%, Mystery Blocksworld FNR 97.09%) and false positives (e.g. Game of 24 FPR 10.4%); it confidently rejects correct answers and accepts wrong ones, so self-verification is unreliable
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode — diagnoses why self-critique fails by measuring LLM-as-verifier accuracy and false-positive/false-negative rates per domain (Table 2) and cataloging critique hallucination types (non-existent edges, hallucinated preconditions, spurious vertex-color claims)
failure_mode_addressed: Exposes 'superficial/unreliable self-reflection' and self-verification miscalibration: high verifier false-negative rates (valid solutions rejected) and false positives, hallucinated critiques, and self-correction error-loops where iterating on self-critique consistently degrades output quality (related to MAST 'superficial self-reflection' / 'incorrect verification' modes)
builds_on: Authors' prior self-verification critiques: Stechly et al. 2023 'GPT-4 Doesn't Know It's Wrong: An Analysis of Iterative Prompting for Reasoning Problems' (arXiv:2310.12397, graph coloring) and Valmeekam et al. planning/PlanBench work; the LLM-Modulo framework (Kambhampati et al.). Critiques the self-critique optimism of Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023), Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al. 2023a), and Weng et al. 2023
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited (~134 citations) by subsequent self-correction critique and verification-scaffolding work, including LLM-Modulo follow-ups, generator-verifier gap analyses, and metacognitive/neuro-symbolic planning agents (e.g. Metagent-P, ACL Findings 2025); broadly grouped with Huang et al. and Kamoi et al. critiques of intrinsic self-correction
reasoning_model_native: no / not-targeted — the study uses GPT-4 (a non-reasoning model, pre-o1/R1) with prompt-engineered iterative self-critique; it does not evaluate reasoning models with built-in reflection, though it is frequently invoked as evidence about the limits of self-verification that motivates testing such models
on_policy_distillation_link: n/a — no distillation or weight-update component; purely inference-time prompting. Relevant only as motivation: it argues improvement signal must come from sound external verification (verifiable reward) rather than the policy's own judgments
sample_efficiency: Iterative self-critique runs up to ~15 backprompt rounds (collapses regardless). Sampling+sound-verifier reaches reported gains at k=15 to k=25 guesses; extending to 150 direct queries + sound verifier reaches 70% on Game of 24 (comparable to ToT's 74% at similar cost)
